facts.statement: Megadontosuchus is an extinct genus of gavialoid crocodile traditionally classified within the subfamily Tomistominae.
facts.quote: Megadontosuchus is an extinct monospecific genus of gavialoid crocodylian, traditionally regarded as a member of Tomistominae

facts.statement: This animal lived during the middle Eocene in Italy.
facts.quote: from the middle Eocene of Italy

facts.statement: Fossils of Megadontosuchus have been found at Monte Duello in the province of Verona.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from Monte Duello in the province of Verona

facts.statement: The genus Megadontosuchus was first erected by paleontologist Charles C. Mook in 1955.
facts.quote: The genus was first erected by paleontologist Charles C. Mook in 1955

facts.statement: The species Megadontosuchus arduini was originally named in 1880 under the genus Crocodilius.
facts.quote: The species was originally named in 1880, although it was assigned to the genus Crocodilius

facts.statement: A lectotype for Megadontosuchus was not proposed until 2007.
Megadontosuchus is distinguished by a robust snout, very large teeth, and large openings on the top of its skull.
facts.quote: Megadontosuchus differs from other traditional "tomistomines" in that it has a more robust rostrum, very large teeth (hence the generic name meaning big-toothed crocodile), and large supratemporal fenestrae on the skull table

facts.statement: Megadontosuchus lived between 41.03 and 37.71 million years ago during the Bartonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Bartonian to Bartonian (41.03 to 37.71 million years ago)
